prompt: Use a doubly bounded type parameter <T extends Number & Comparable<T>> to write spread, average and aboveAverage so one copy of the code works for List<Integer>, List<Double> and List<Long>.
explanation: An intersection bound lists several supertypes with &, and inside the method T is treated as having all of them, so doubleValue() (from Number) and compareTo (from Comparable) are both legal. Because the bound is checked at the call site, List<String> simply will not compile -- the safety is free. Rounding with Math.round(mean * 100.0) / 100.0 keeps the returned doubles exactly comparable in the tests, while aboveAverage deliberately compares against the unrounded mean.
hints: The header is public static <T extends Number & Comparable<T>> double spread(List<T> values) -- Number must come first, and only one class is allowed in the bound.
Track the smallest and largest with two T variables seeded from values.get(0), then compare with value.compareTo(smallest) < 0.
Handle the empty list before any get(0) call, and remember aboveAverage uses the raw mean, not the rounded one.
